name: Humerus Desolate
description: Humerus Desolate is a dead world stripped bare by eons of exposure. Its surface is a monotonous grey expanse of impact craters and erosion channels, with the planet's metallic core exposed along a long equatorial wound where the crust was torn away by some ancient catastrophe. The exposed core gleams dull silver in the starlight, a bone-like ridge running the length of the world like the shaft of an enormous humerus.

Without atmosphere, the planet exists in absolute silence, and the temperature extremes crack the surface into a web of fissures that spread with glacial slowness. The core exposure creates a weak magnetic field that funnels solar particles into visible streamers at the wound's edges, the only dynamic feature on an otherwise static world. Standing on the surface, the stillness is so complete it feels like time itself has abandoned this place.

A graveyard of defunct satellites and decommissioned probes orbits Humerus Desolate, accumulated over centuries of use as a disposal site for obsolete orbital hardware. The practice was discontinued when it became clear the debris field posed a navigation hazard, but the existing hardware remains. Some of the older satellites contain technology from eras and civilizations no longer extant, making them objects of historical and technical interest.

The exposed core is rich in metals of exceptional purity, easily accessible for surface mining operations. The satellite graveyard offers salvage opportunities for those willing to navigate the debris field, with the oldest units potentially containing technology that predates current civilizational memory. The planet's utter desolation makes it psychologically challenging for extended stays, and mining crews rotate on short schedules to prevent the isolation-related incidents that marked early operations.
